definition: The tradition of giving numbers symbolic meanings and working them out from dates or names. In this app it is treated as a tool for reflection and entertainment, not as a scientific method.
Adding the digits of a number until a single digit remains, e.g. 38 → 3 + 8 = 11 → 1 + 1 = 2. In the convention used here, reduction stops at master numbers wherever they are allowed.
The conventional name for the numbers 11, 22 and 33, which many schools of numerology do not reduce further. It is a label from the tradition, not a sign that a person is superior or exceptional.

A number worked out from the full date of birth, which in the tradition describes the general theme or direction of a life. The app adds all the digits of the date and then reduces the sum, keeping 11, 22 and 33.
A number worked out from the day of the month on which someone was born. The tradition links it with a natural talent or style of acting; the app keeps 11 and 22.
A number worked out from all the letters of the full name. It describes symbolically how someone shows their abilities to the outside world.
A number worked out from the vowels in the full name. In the tradition it refers to inner motivations and needs.
A number worked out from the consonants in the full name. It symbolises the first impression and the outer layer that others see.

term: Vowels and consonants in this convention
definition: The app treats the letters A, E, I, O, U and Y as vowels and all the others as consonants. Other schools treat the letter Y differently, so results may differ.

Replacing letters with Polish diacritics by their base equivalents before the calculation, e.g. Ą → A, Ł → L, Ż → Z. This is because the traditional table covers only the 26 letters of the Latin alphabet.

The table most widely used today, which gives the letters A–Z values from 1 to 9 in a repeating cycle (A = 1 … I = 9, J = 1 … R = 9, S = 1 … Z = 8). Despite its name it is a modern system, not the work of the ancient Pythagoreans.

A number from 1 to 9 worked out from the day and month of birth and a chosen calendar year. In the tradition it describes the theme of that year within a nine-year cycle; in the app it is an invitation to reflect, not a forecast.
The idea that personal years follow one another from 1 to 9, after which the cycle starts again. It is a symbolic model that gives reflection a structure.
The name of a strand of interpretation that combines number symbolism with the language of self-reflection. It is not a psychological or clinical method and is not used for diagnosis.
A deck of usually 78 cards, originally used for games and, since the 18th century, also in esoteric practice. In the app the cards are images that prompt reflection.
The 22 trump cards of the tarot, each with its own name and image, e.g. The Fool, The Magician, The Sun. The tradition links them with the broad themes of life.
56 cards divided into four suits, with cards from ace to ten and the court cards. The tradition links them with everyday matters and situations.
One of the four series of the Minor Arcana: Wands (Rods, Staves), Cups (Chalices), Swords and Pentacles (Coins, Disks). Each suit has a symbolic area assigned to it in the tradition.
The Minor Arcana cards that show figures: Page (Knave), Knight, Queen and King. They are often read as styles of acting or roles rather than as specific people.
A card that comes out upside down when laid. Some people read it as a different or muted take on the card's theme; others do not use reversals at all.

A layout of several cards in which each position has a meaning or a question assigned to it, e.g. background, challenge, possible step. In the app the positions are questions for reflection, not predictions.
A tarot deck published in London in 1909 by Rider, prepared under the direction of A. E. Waite and illustrated by Pamela Colman Smith. Its images influenced many later decks.
The Italian name for the playing cards from which tarot developed, known since the 15th century. They were originally used for a social game with trump cards.
A universal pattern of character or situation that recurs in myths, stories and culture, e.g. the Hero or the Sage. In the app archetypes are a tool for reflection, not a personality typology.
A conventional term for the less helpful sides of a pattern, which may appear when its traits are exaggerated. The shadow description is there to prompt thought, not judgement.
A term introduced by C. G. Jung for meaningful coincidences of events with no causal link. In the context of cards it is often used loosely; it is not evidence that divination works.
